summary: Forgotten Missions is an interactive scroll-story website that lets 13 NASA machines left on the Moon and Mars tell their own stories: six Apollo landers and seven Mars landers and rovers. Each chapter pairs a real NASA photo with a short story in the machine's own voice, narrated by our team. A Learn more panel explains, in simple language for young students, why each mission was built, what it found, its timeline and what happened to the equipment. An explore-every-site map, built on NASA's Moon and Mars maps, shows each landing site with photo markers and a "left behind by year" slider. It helps students and teachers learn space history in a way they remember, and it points to the NASA sources behind every fact.
details:
CHALLENGE

Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars.

WHY (THE PROBLEM)

Space history is told through launches. The endings are hard to find: they sit in catalogs and datasets written for scientists, not for students. Six Apollo landers and many Mars landers and rovers are still where they were left, and most students have never heard what happened to them.

WHAT WE BUILT

Forgotten Missions is a scroll-story website with 13 chapters: Apollo 11, 12, 14, 15, 16 and 17 on the Moon, and Viking 1, Viking 2, Mars Pathfinder (Sojourner), Spirit, Opportunity, Phoenix and Mars Polar Lander on Mars.

- Scroll story: each chapter pins a real NASA photo. After a short scroll, the machine tells its own story in a text bubble and our recorded voice plays.

- Learn more panel: why the mission was built, what it found, a timeline, and what happened to the equipment, in simple language for young students, with an optional read-aloud button.

- Built to last vs actually lasted: animated bars comparing the planned and real working time of five Mars missions.

- Explore every site: a NASA Moon or Mars map with photo markers, a site list, a "left behind by year" slider, and links between the map and the chapters.

- A progress bar and chapter dots for navigation, reduced-motion support and keyboard-friendly buttons.

HOW IT WORKS

All content comes from one data file (missions, coordinates, dates, story text, NASA sources) and one file of student-friendly details. A small Node script downloads photos from the NASA Image and Video Library and records their IDs, which are shown on screen as credits. The site is static (React and Vite) and runs in any browser. Adding a new mission takes one data entry.

WHO IT HELPS AND ITS IMPACT

Students, teachers and space fans. It turns hard-to-find mission endings into short stories that students remember, and it points them to the NASA sources behind each fact. It is free, open source and designed to work in any browser.

WHAT WE WOULD BUILD NEXT

More missions, including hardware from other space agencies, and more languages; classroom activities and quizzes; real archive footage in each chapter; an expert review of every fact; and 3D views of the landing sites.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

React, Vite, Leaflet, GSAP (ScrollTrigger), JavaScript, CSS, Node.js, Vercel.

USE OF SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI)

- Code and data: the website code, the photo-download script and the simple-language rewrites of our own facts were written with help from Claude (Anthropic) in claude.ai. This is stated in our README and in the header of each code file.

- Images and videos: no image or video was generated by SI. All photos and maps are from NASA and USGS.

- Audio: the narration was recorded by our team. The optional "Read this to me" button uses the browser's built-in speech synthesis.

- Our team chose the story, checked the facts against NASA sources, and tested the site.

LINKS

Live site: https://forgottenmission-kappa.vercel.app/

Code: https://github.com/imtiaz-zihad/Forgotten-Mission

Extended 240-second walkthrough: https://youtu.be/R8SQQnK0Dn0
